newsitem.title: INDIA: India buys 8.85 mln T wheat for stocks by June 10.
newsitem.headline: India buys 8.85 mln T wheat for stocks by June 10.

text.p: Indian agencies had bought 8.85 million tonnes of wheat from farmers up to June 10 for sale in the 1997/98 (April-March) season compared with 8.1 million on the same date last year, an Agriculture Ministry spokesman said on Thursday.
The government buys wheat to build up its buffer stocks, which it then uses to control prices by releasing stocks through a state-run distribution system.
Total arrivals in the domestic markets were about 10.5 million tonnes up to June 10 compared with nine million on the same date in 1996, the spokesman said.
The government said earlier this month state agencies were expected to buy about 11.1 million tonnes of wheat for sale in 1997/98 compared with 8.2 million for 1996/97.
Government buying started late this year and is expected to last until end-June.
